analysis:
Examined two base-text excerpts (lines 13587-15248) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. These are public synthetic test vectors for the prompt contract (token IDs, chain hashes, template input). No secrets, credentials or consumer data are present; the content is repeated public placeholder text such as 'Public followup.' and 'Public synthetic cache-parity input.'. The supplied excerpts are base-side only and sit outside the changed ranges, which begin at base lines 43813 and in the 3000-4000 range. Their only relevance is surrounding context for the vector set.

The patch excerpt, which is truncated, shows a change to a Qwen-style vector: it adds additional_context.enable_thinking=false to template_input, shrinks prompt_token_count from 803 to 767, and changes the prefix-cache chain hashes and block boundaries. The effect is a fixture-level update to the prompt-contract and cache-block chain hashes, and a 768-token block boundary is dropped. This relates to T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing) only as a test-vector contract. The change does not alter runtime code, authorization, attestation or encryption paths (TB-002, TB-011), and no regression is evident from the supplied evidence.

Open integration questions: the production code (Swift provider and coordinator) that consumes these vectors was not supplied. Whether prompt_contract_id values and chain hashes are kept consistent between provider and coordinator, and whether the prefix-cache keying still includes scope_id, is unverified. The remaining changed vector hunks (head lines ~3805, 3904, 4752, 43739, 44524, 45471, 52354, 53139, 54086) were not in my units. I raise no findings. needs_deeper_review is set false because these units contain only inert fixtures.
